summary.title: Config Drift and Attack Path Agent
summary.description: A cloud platform that monitors configuration drift and analyzes configuration weaknesses using AI (Amazon Bedrock), maps attack paths and generates remediations.

data.name: User (Browser)
data.description: Corporate user who views reports and triggers scans via the web frontend

data.name: External APIs
data.description: External API data source for network/security configurations (https://api.radwarecloud.app/v1/gms/applications)

data.name: Corporate Proxy
data.description: Outbound proxy (vsearray.intra.absaafrica:80) for external API access

data.name: Fargate (API + UI)
data.description: ECS Fargate container serving frontend UI and API endpoints (/api/scan, /api/reports, /api/reports/:id) behind Internal ALB

threats.title: 1.1 Session token theft / credential impersonation
threats.description: Attacker steals session token or credentials to impersonate legitimate user, gaining unauthorized access to security reports and attack paths.
threats.mitigation: Corporate SSO (SAML/OIDC). Short-lived session tokens. HttpOnly/Secure cookies.

threats.title: 1.2 API parameter manipulation
threats.description: User manipulates API request parameters (source IDs, report IDs) via browser tools to trigger scans on unintended targets or access unauthorized reports.
threats.mitigation: Input validation. Allowlist source IDs against Parameter Store. Request body schema validation.

threats.title: 1.3 User denies triggering scan or downloading report
threats.description: User triggers scan or downloads sensitive report, then denies it. No accountability for system misuse or data exfiltration.
threats.mitigation: ALB access logs + CloudTrail + application audit log (user identity, action, timestamp).

threats.title: 1.4 Reports/attack paths exposed to unauthorized users
threats.description: Reports containing weaknesses and attack paths exposed to unauthorized users via shared URLs, cached content, or over-broad access. Provides exploitation roadmap for attackers.
threats.mitigation: Auth required on all endpoints. S3 pre-signed URLs with 5-min TTL. No-cache headers. Scoped access per team/source.

threats.title: 1.5 Scan spam floods pipeline
threats.description: User spams POST /api/scan flooding pipeline executions causing resource exhaustion, cost spike, and Bedrock throttling.
threats.mitigation: Rate limiting per user on Fargate API. Step Function concurrency limit. AWS budget alerts.

threats.title: 1.6 Normal user accesses admin functions
threats.description: Normal user accesses admin functions (trigger scans, modify sources, delete reports) leading to unauthorized config changes, data loss, or unnecessary scan costs.
threats.mitigation: RBAC enforced in Fargate app. Role claims from SSO token validated per endpoint. Least-privilege IAM on Fargate task role.

data.name: Step Functions
data.description: Orchestrates 8 Lambdas sequentially with Map state for parallel per-source execution and Choice state for drift detection branching

threats.title: 2.1 Unauthorized StartExecution call
threats.description: Unauthorized entity calls StartExecution on Step Function causing rogue pipeline executions, resource consumption, and cost.
threats.mitigation: IAM restricts StartExecution to EventBridge role + Fargate task role only, scoped to specific State Machine ARN.

threats.title: 2.5 Cannot prove what Lambda/Bedrock did
threats.description: Lambda modifies/deletes data or Bedrock call produces incorrect results — cannot prove what happened. Cannot diagnose false negatives or root cause data changes.
threats.mitigation: Structured JSON logging per Lambda (metadata only). CloudTrail data events. Step Function execution history (immutable). Log Bedrock request IDs + token counts.

threats.title: 2.8 Lambda timeout / infinite retry / Bedrock throttling
threats.description: Lambda hangs on unresponsive service, infinite retry, or Bedrock throttling causing cost spike, pipeline stuck, resource exhaustion.
threats.mitigation: Lambda timeout (hard cap). Step Function state timeout. Retry limits with backoff. Map state MaxConcurrency. CloudWatch alarms on duration/errors.

data.name: Ingestion Lambda
data.description: Fetches configs from external sources (Radware, AD) via corporate proxy, stores raw config in S3

threats.title: 2.2 Lambda code modified to skip security checks
threats.description: Lambda code modified to skip security checks or falsify reports (early return, altered logic). False sense of security, silent posture degradation.
threats.mitigation: CI/CD with approval gates. Lambda CodeSigning. Lambda versioning. CloudTrail alerts on UpdateFunctionCode. Only CI/CD role can deploy.

threats.title: 4.2 MITM between Lambda and Radware API
threats.description: Man-in-the-middle between Lambda and Radware API via proxy. Modified config response leads to false analysis throughout pipeline.
threats.mitigation: TLS end-to-end (HTTPS). Certificate validation (verify=True). Pin certificates if possible.

threats.title: 4.4 API keys visible in transit or proxy logs
threats.description: API keys visible in transit or proxy logs leading to credential theft.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS (proxy sees destination, not headers/body). Secrets fetched at runtime from Secrets Manager, never in env vars or code.

threats.title: 4.5 Corporate proxy outage blocks config ingestion
threats.description: Corporate proxy outage blocks all config ingestion. No configs fetched, no drift detection, monitoring gap.
threats.mitigation: CloudWatch alarm on Ingest Lambda failures. Escalation runbook to network team.

threats.title: 4.6 Lambda gains broader corporate network access
threats.description: Lambda gains access to broader corporate network via VPN tunnel enabling lateral movement to internal systems.
threats.mitigation: Security groups restrict Lambda ENIs to proxy IP:port only. No broad corporate CIDR access. Network ACLs as secondary control.

data.name: Hash and Diff Lambdas
data.description: Computes config hashes for drift detection and generates diffs between current and previous configs

threats.title: 2.9 Lambda role over-permissioned
threats.description: Single Lambda role has excessive permissions across all S3 prefixes, DynamoDB tables, and Bedrock. One compromised Lambda = full system compromise.
threats.mitigation: Separate IAM role per Lambda. Each scoped to specific S3 prefixes, DynamoDB actions, and Bedrock access. Principle of least privilege.

data.name: Bedrock Analysis
data.description: Lambdas that call Amazon Bedrock (Claude Sonnet, temperature 0) for security check, attack paths, and remediation generation

threats.title: 2.3 [P1] Prompt injection via malicious config content
threats.description: HIGHEST PRIORITY THREAT. Malicious content embedded in config manipulates Bedrock into reporting 'no issues found'. Attacker hides vulnerabilities from detection. Entire report is falsified.
threats.mitigation: Separate data from instructions in prompt. Structured JSON output schema. Output validation (zero findings on 50k-line config = suspicious). Input sanitization. Bedrock Guardrails. Prompt delimiters (<CONFIG_START>...<CONFIG_END>).

threats.title: 2.4 Bedrock returns malformed/empty response
threats.description: Bedrock returns malformed/empty response, stored as-is. Misleading report, garbage data presented to users.
threats.mitigation: Validate Bedrock response schema before storing. Reject empty/malformed responses. Step Function error handler on validation failure.

threats.title: 2.6 Lambda logs contain sensitive config data
threats.description: Lambda logs or Step Function state contain sensitive config data (credentials, IPs). Credential exposure via CloudWatch Logs or execution history.
threats.mitigation: Never log raw configs — log metadata only. Custom regex sanitization layer. CloudWatch Logs encrypted with KMS. Minimize sensitive data in Step Function state payloads.

threats.title: 2.7 Sensitive config data sent to Bedrock
threats.description: Sensitive config data (credentials, internal IPs) sent to Bedrock. Data exposure, compliance failure, echoed in reports.
threats.mitigation: Regex sanitization before every Bedrock call. Enterprise Bedrock (data stays in account). Bedrock invocation logs encrypted + restricted.

data.name: Report Lambda
data.description: Compiles final security report from analysis outputs and stores in S3 reports/ prefix

data.name: KMS
data.description: AWS Key Management Service - CMK for SSE-KMS encryption of all data at rest (S3, DynamoDB, CloudWatch Logs)

threats.title: 5.4 KMS key policy modified for broader access
threats.description: KMS key policy modified to grant broader decryption access. Unauthorized decryption of all encrypted data.
threats.mitigation: CloudTrail alerts on PutKeyPolicy/CreateGrant. Key policy changes require admin. IaC drift detection.

threats.title: 5.6 [P7] KMS key scheduled for deletion
threats.description: CATASTROPHIC: KMS key scheduled for deletion makes all encrypted data permanently inaccessible. Permanent data loss.
threats.mitigation: 7-30 day mandatory waiting period. CloudTrail alert on ScheduleKeyDeletion. Restrict to break-glass admin role only.

data.name: HTTPS: Scan/Report requests
data.description: User sends scan requests and retrieves reports via HTTPS

data.name: EventBridge
data.description: Triggers scheduled scans via cron rule targeting Step Functions

threats.title: 5.1 [P9] EventBridge rule disabled — silent monitoring gap
threats.description: EventBridge rule disabled/deleted so no scheduled scans run. Drift goes undetected indefinitely. Silent monitoring gap.
threats.mitigation: CloudWatch alarm on 'zero executions in 24h'. CloudTrail alert on DeleteRule/DisableRule. IaC drift detection.

data.name: S3
data.description: Single bucket with prefix separation: configs/, reports/, remediations/. SSE-KMS encrypted. VPC endpoint access only.

threats.title: 3.1 Stolen credentials access S3
threats.description: Attacker accesses S3 with stolen credentials. Reads configs, reports, attack paths. Manipulates hashes.
threats.mitigation: VPC Endpoint policy (non-VPC access denied). Bucket policy enforces aws:SourceVpc. No public access. IAM scoped per Lambda to specific prefixes.

threats.title: 3.2 Config or report modified/deleted after storage
threats.description: Config or report modified/deleted after storage. Attacker hides evidence. Integrity of security analysis compromised.
threats.mitigation: S3 Versioning. S3 Object Lock (compliance mode) for reports. MFA Delete. CloudTrail S3 data events.

threats.title: 3.5 [P4] Raw configs or attack path reports leaked
threats.description: Raw configs or attack path reports leaked. Attacker gains infrastructure knowledge + exploitation roadmap.
threats.mitigation: SSE-KMS encryption (CMK). Block Public Access. Pre-signed URLs with short TTL. VPC-only access via endpoint policy. Per-Lambda prefix scoping.

threats.title: 3.6 S3 flooded or DynamoDB throttled
threats.description: S3 flooded with large objects causing financial impact, pipeline blocked, frontend can't list reports.
threats.mitigation: S3 Lifecycle policies. DynamoDB on-demand capacity. Budget alerts. Lambda write size validation.

data.name: DynamoDB
data.description: Stores config hashes (drift detection), S3 key references, and report metadata

threats.title: 3.3 [P2] Hash tampering bypasses drift detection
threats.description: CRITICAL: Stored hash modified to match compromised config. Drift detection silently bypassed. Attacker changes config AND hash, system reports 'no drift'.
threats.mitigation: Only Hash Lambda role has PutItem on hash table. DynamoDB Streams for change audit. CloudTrail data events. Alert on unexpected hash changes.

threats.title: 3.4 DynamoDB records modified with no trace
threats.description: S3 objects or DynamoDB records modified/deleted with no trace. Cannot attribute data changes.
threats.mitigation: S3 access logging + CloudTrail data events. DynamoDB Streams → archive to S3 (immutable). Point-in-time recovery. MFA Delete.

threats.title: 3.7 Cross-prefix/table access via IAM misconfiguration
threats.description: Lambda with configs/* write also writes to reports/*. Fargate writes hashes (should only read metadata). Data integrity violation.
threats.mitigation: IAM per Lambda scoped to specific prefixes. Separate DynamoDB tables or fine-grained access.

data.name: Secrets Manager
data.description: Stores API credentials (x-api-key, Context headers) for Radware and other external sources

threats.title: 5.3 [P6] Secret value tampered — redirects to attacker API
threats.description: Secret value modified to redirect auth to attacker's API. Poisoned config ingestion via attacker-controlled endpoint.
threats.mitigation: Restrict PutSecretValue to admin roles (Lambdas read-only). CloudTrail alerts on secret changes. Secrets versioning for rollback.

threats.title: 5.5 Secrets exposed in Lambda env vars or logs
threats.description: Secrets exposed in Lambda env vars, logs, or error messages. Credential theft, external system compromise.
threats.mitigation: Secrets fetched at runtime via SDK (never env vars). Sanitization prevents logging. Error messages redact secrets.

threats.title: 5.7 Secret rotation fails — pipeline breaks silently
threats.description: Secret rotation fails or parameters deleted causing pipeline to break silently. Ingestion fails, no new scans, monitoring gap.
threats.mitigation: CloudWatch alarms on rotation failures, auth errors, zero sources returned. IaC backs up parameter values.

data.name: ECR
data.description: Elastic Container Registry storing Fargate container images

threats.title: 6.1 [P5] Malicious container image pushed
threats.description: Attacker pushes malicious container image tagged as legitimate, or impersonates CI/CD to deploy code. Backdoor in Lambda or Fargate container — full application compromise.
threats.mitigation: ECR immutable tags. Image signing (AWS Signer). IAM restricts ecr:PutImage + Lambda deploy to CI/CD role only. CI/CD authenticates via OIDC (no long-lived creds).

threats.title: 6.2 Malicious dependency via supply chain
threats.description: Malicious dependency injected via supply chain (pip, npm). Backdoor in Lambda layer or container — data exfiltration, credential theft.
threats.mitigation: Dependency pinning with hashes. Dependency scanning (Dependabot/Snyk). ECR image scan on push. Private PyPI mirror if available.

threats.title: 6.5 Container image contains hardcoded secrets
threats.description: Container image contains hardcoded secrets or CI/CD logs expose credentials.
threats.mitigation: No secrets in Dockerfile. Use Secrets Manager at runtime. CI/CD secret masking. Build logs access-restricted.

threats.title: 6.6 ECR images deleted — cannot deploy or scale
threats.description: ECR images deleted or CI/CD unavailable. Application unavailable, cannot respond to incidents.
threats.mitigation: ECR lifecycle retains last N images. IAM restricts image deletion to admin. Multiple deployment paths (manual fallback).

threats.title: 6.7 CI/CD deployment role overly broad
threats.description: CI/CD deployment role or Fargate execution role has overly broad permissions. Compromised pipeline/container can modify IAM, delete resources, access all data.
threats.mitigation: Deployment role scoped to Lambda update + ECR push + ECS deploy only. Fargate execution role: ECR pull only. Permission boundaries.

data.name: Parameter Store
data.description: Stores source endpoint URLs and configuration for which systems to monitor

threats.title: 5.2 [P3] Parameter Store poisoned — malicious source URL
threats.description: Parameter Store poisoned — malicious source URL added or existing one modified. Ingest Lambda fetches from attacker-controlled endpoint. Poisoned config enters entire pipeline.
threats.mitigation: IAM restricts ssm:PutParameter to admin only (no Lambda writes). CloudTrail alerts on changes. Domain whitelist validation in Get Sources Lambda. IaC drift detection.

data.name: StartExecution (source list)

data.name: Invoke: Ingest config

data.name: HTTPS: GET config via proxy
data.description: Ingestion Lambda fetches raw config from Radware API through corporate proxy. ~50k line JSON response.

threats.title: 4.1 Rogue resource impersonates legitimate traffic
threats.description: Rogue resource impersonates legitimate traffic to corporate proxy for unauthorized external API access.
threats.mitigation: Security groups restrict outbound to proxy IP:port only. VPC Flow Logs.

threats.title: 4.3 Cannot identify which Lambda made external call
threats.description: Cannot identify which Lambda made which external call. No attribution for external API interactions.
threats.mitigation: VPC Flow Logs + structured Lambda logging (source, endpoint, timestamp, request ID).
